Since the app uses global interactivity, all pages are interactive by default. To make specific pages static SSR so they can access HttpContext, I need to use the `[ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]` attribute on the account pages - though I'm second-guessing whether that's the right attribute name in .NET 8+.

The real issue is that when a component renders interactively via SignalR, there's no HTTP request context, so HttpContext becomes null. Microsoft's standard solution is to use static SSR for auth pages by not applying the interactive render mode to them. But since the app has global interactivity set on `<Routes>`, I need a different approach - either configure render modes per-page instead of globally, or use minimal API endpoints for the login and register flows. out of interactive routing when using global interactivity. The `@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]` attribute forces a full page navigation instead of using the interactive router, which makes HttpContext available for those pages.

I'm recalling how the official .NET 8 Blazor Identity template actually structures this - it seems like the approach involves configuring the render mode at the app level and then selectively opting pages out of interactivity rather than the other way around. Right, so the pattern uses `HttpContext.AcceptsInteractiveRouting()` to conditionally apply the render mode in `App.razor`, and pages marked with `[ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]` will render as static SSR since that method returns false for them.

Now I need to set up the project structure: adding the Identity and Entity Framework packages, creating the user and database context classes, then updating `Program.cs` to wire everything together.

For the UI, I'll mark the account pages with `[ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]` so they stay static, create a logout endpoint as a minimal API, and update the layout to display authentication status with login/logout links.

Completing the login handler that attempts authentication and navigates on success, with a sealed class defining the email and password input fields that have validation attributes. I'm also noting that for static SSR pages, forcing a page reload after login ensures the authentication cookie gets properly sent with subsequent requests. With `BlazorDisableThrowNavigationException` enabled, `NavigateTo` won't trigger the navigation exception during static SSR, so I need to use `HttpContext.Response.Redirect()` instead. I can access `HttpContext` as a cascading parameter in the Razor component and call redirect directly after the login succeeds. I think the flag only affects interactive rendering, so `NavigationManager.NavigateTo` with `forceLoad: true` should work fine in static SSR. I'll go with that approach since it matches the official template. For the logout endpoint, I'll create a minimal API POST handler since that's the simplest approach, and then I need to think through how the navigation will work in the interactive `MainLayout`.

To display the auth state in the nav, I'll use the `AuthorizeView` component, which works in interactive mode since Identity provides the `AuthenticationStateProvider`. I also need to register `AddCascadingAuthenticationState()` in the service configuration to make the auth state available as a cascading parameter throughout the app.

Clean build. Here's a summary of what was done:

### The core problem & solution
`SignInManager`/`UserManager` need `HttpContext`, which isn't available in interactive server components (they run over SignalR). The fix: **`[ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]`** on auth pages + conditional render mode in `App.razor`. Auth pages render as static SSR (with full HTTP context), while everything else stays globally interactive.

### Files created
- **`Data/ApplicationUser.cs`** — `IdentityUser` subclass
- **`Data/ApplicationDbContext.cs`** — `IdentityDbContext<ApplicationUser>` with in-memory EF
- **`Components/Pages/Account/Login.razor`** — static SSR login with `EditForm`, validation, redirects to `/`
- **`Components/Pages/Account/Register.razor`** — static SSR register with confirm-password, redirects to `/account/login`

### Files modified
- **`Program.cs`** — Identity services, EF in-memory, auth middleware, `MapPost("/account/logout")` endpoint
- **`App.razor`** — uses `HttpContext.AcceptsInteractiveRouting()` to conditionally apply `InteractiveServer` render mode
- **`MainLayout.razor`** — `<AuthorizeView>` in top bar showing "Logged in as {email} | Logout" or "Login | Register"
- **`_Imports.razor`** — added auth-related usings

### How the logout works
It's a minimal API `POST` endpoint (`/account/logout`) that calls `SignInManager.SignOutAsync()` — no Blazor component needed, so the `HttpContext` issue is sidestepped entirely. The nav uses a plain `<form>` with an antiforgery token to POST to it.
